records.failureSummary: Implemented escapeHtml and escapeAttribute in src/render.mjs per AC-05, together with the render-page helpers they support (renderInline, renderMarkdownLite, renderPage), since every AC-05 test exercises the escaping through renderPage. escapeHtml coerces non-string input at the trust boundary and replaces & first, then < > \" and ' with & < > " ', using only String.prototype.replace with regex-escaped literals (no third-party dependency). escapeAttribute applies the same ampersand-first escaping to URL values so a URL cannot break out of a double-quoted href attribute. renderPage preserves the documented API contract (single page object, returns a complete HTML document string; escapeHtml, escapeAttribute, renderPage are named exports) and safely handles null/non-object page and null/non-string title/body. Only the backend file src/render.mjs was changed; no test files were touched. Verified: node --test test/render.ac05.test.mjs reports 7 tests, 7 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors (all T-05 AC-05 tests green); npm run build and npm run lint both exit 0. The full npm run test reports 31 tests, 29 passed, 2 failed, 0 errors. The two residual failures are outside this backend slice: (1) test/build.test.mjs still fails because buildSite in src/build.mjs remains an unimplemented stub owned by a separate task; (2) one assertion in the T-06 combined test test/render.combined.test.mjs line 164 is mutually unsatisfiable with line 157 of the same test and cannot be made green by any spec-compliant escapeAttribute, so it requires a QA-side test fix.
